0.long_answer: Barth syndrome is primarily linked to mutations in the TAZ gene, which is located on the X chromosome. However, in the search for treatments to address the cardiolipin abnormalities seen in Barth syndrome, another target has been proposed. Research has suggested that modulating the activity of iPLA2‐VIA, a gene located on the p arm of chromosome 22, could offer therapeutic benefit. iPLA2‐VIA encodes a calcium‐independent phospholipase A2 enzyme that plays a role in lipid remodeling. By targeting this gene, it may be possible to improve the abnormal cardiolipin metabolism that underlies many of the symptoms seen in Barth syndrome.
